title: B2+ · L13 — News broadcasting style
description: Comprender e imitar el estilo de noticias en ingles: voz pasiva, headlines en presente, formulas de reportero.

questions.prompt: Escribes el titular para BBC News sobre una firma reciente de ley climatica.
questions.question: Choose the correct news-style headline:
options: The president signed a bill yesterday.
Bill was signed by the president.
questions.explanation: Los headlines siguen 'headlinese' — un dialecto especifico: PRESENTE SIMPLE para eventos pasados recientes (crea dramatismo e inmediatez), omision de articulos ('the'), verbos cortos y activos, adjetivos como 'landmark' (historico/hito). Regla del NYT/BBC: cada palabra debe cargar significado. 'Yesterday' se sobreentiende — nunca aparece en headline. Registro: universal en periodicos anglo — el que domina headlinese domina lectura rapida de noticias.
examples: Fed cuts interest rates by half a point. → economics headline typical
Tech giant acquires rival in landmark deal. → M&A headline standard

questions.prompt: Escribes el primer parrafo (lead) de la noticia del terremoto en Peru.
questions.question: Which is the strongest news lead (opening sentence)?
options: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck coastal Peru early Tuesday, killing at least 45 and displacing thousands.
questions.explanation: News lead sigue la 'inverted pyramid': cinco W's (who/what/when/where + how) + numero especifico + impacto humano, todo en UNA frase densa. 'Struck' (verbo dramatico corto), 'killing at least' (attribucion cauta con numero minimo verificado), 'displacing thousands' (impacto colateral). Estilo AP/Reuters. Error hispano: leads largos con contexto historico primero — el estilo anglo pone las CONSECUENCIAS primero, contexto despues. Registro: news wire estandar mundial.
examples: A cyber attack disrupted operations at 12 major hospitals across Germany, forcing the cancellation of surgeries. → cyber news lead
Wildfires tore through Northern California overnight, destroying 200 homes and displacing 8,000 residents. → disaster lead

questions.statement: Passive voice is heavily used in news reporting to focus on the event rather than the actor.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. La voz pasiva es SIGNATURE del news style — 'Three people were arrested', 'The bill has been passed', 'A statement was issued'. Dos razones: (1) focaliza el EVENTO/RESULTADO, no al actor (mas relevante para lector); (2) evita atribucion problematica cuando la responsabilidad no esta confirmada legalmente. Contraste con creative writing (activa preferida). Registro: passive news style contraria a la regla escolar 'evita la pasiva' — en news es correcto. Error hispano: escribir noticias en activa constantemente, suena a blog personal.
examples: The suspect was taken into custody late Monday. → foco en resultado, no en quien
A ceasefire has been agreed by all parties. → uso del by cuando la fuente importa

questions.prompt: Lees un articulo de investigacion: 'Sources close to the White House say a resignation is imminent.'
questions.question: In news English, 'Sources say...' typically means:
options: Information from unnamed but credible informants.
questions.explanation: 'Sources say' / 'according to sources' es formula estandar para info verificada de informantes NO IDENTIFICADOS publicamente. Politica editorial rigurosa (NYT, WaPo, Reuters): requiere MINIMO 2 fuentes independientes verificadas antes de publicar. Diferentes gradientes de confianza: 'sources familiar with the matter' (medio), 'sources close to X' (alto), 'a person briefed on the discussions' (indirecto). Error hispano: interpretar como especulacion — es lo contrario, es info verificada pero anonimizada por proteccion de la fuente.
examples: Sources close to the negotiations say a deal is imminent. → alta confianza
According to two people familiar with the matter... → doble sourcing

questions.text: Officials have declined to comment, citing the ongoing nature of the investigation.
questions.explanation: Formulismo tipico de noticias para reportar el silencio oficial. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'have declined' con weak /əvdɪˈklaɪnd/; 'to comment' con weak /təˈkɒmənt/; 'ongoing' con /ɒnˈɡəʊɪŋ/. Colocaciones nativas del news style: 'declined to comment' (rechazaron comentar — formal), 'citing X' (aduciendo X — participio de razon), 'ongoing investigation' (investigacion en curso — colocacion fija). Neutralidad periodistica: reportar la no-respuesta sin juicio.
examples: The company declined to comment, pointing to a pending SEC review.
Authorities have not confirmed the reports, citing operational security.

questions.prompt: Titular sobre reaccion politica a un atentado.
questions.question: Which verb is MOST typical of news headlines?
questions.explanation: Verbos de headlinese — cortos, dramaticos, en presente: VOWS (promete solemnemente), PLEDGES (compromete), SLAMS (critica duramente), URGES (insta), HAILS (elogia), UNVEILS (revela/lanza), SPARKS (desencadena), BLASTS (critica ferozmente), MULLS (considera), EYES (busca/analiza). Estos verbos existen en headlinese casi exclusivamente — en spoken serian raros. Diseno: cada verbo es de 3-5 letras, cabe en headline space, y transmite emocion sin ambiguedad. Registro: universal en periodicos anglo (Guardian, NYT, WaPo, BBC).
examples: President vows swift response to attack. → 'vow' = compromiso solemne
CEO hails record quarter as 'turning point'. → 'hail' = celebrar publicamente

questions.prompt: Empareja cada termino de vocabulario periodistico con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Seis terminos periodisticos indispensables. 'Alleged' es palabra LEGAL clave — protege al medio de demandas por difamacion (implica presuncion de inocencia). Politica editorial obligatoria: no puedes decir 'the killer' hasta condena firme; usas 'the alleged killer' o 'the suspect'. 'Death toll' es la cuantificacion oficial. 'Landmark' se reserva para eventos historicos genuinos (no todo caso judicial). Todos son universales US/UK.
examples: The alleged perpetrator was arraigned Monday. → uso legal preciso
In a landmark ruling, the Supreme Court decided that... → uso historico calibrado

questions.target: In breaking news tonight — a major cybersecurity breach has been reported at one of the country's largest banks, potentially affecting millions of customers.
questions.explanation: Opening classico de news broadcast TV nocturno. 'In breaking news tonight' (opener signature de nightly news US), 'has been reported' (present perfect passivo — hedge de responsabilidad), 'potentially affecting' (hedging factual — no confirmado el numero exacto), 'millions' (magnitud sin especificar precision). Ritmo natural: pausa dramatica marcada en el guion largo (—), tono descendente firme, sin acelerar. Contracciones: 'country's' pero no 'has' — 'has' se mantiene completo en news formal.
examples: Coming up next: a developing story out of Washington. → cliffhanger a break comercial
Just in — officials have confirmed the identity of the suspect. → 'just in' = ahora mismo

questions.prompt: El anchor dice: 'This is a developing story — we'll bring you updates as they come in.'
questions.question: 'Developing story' means:
options: News that is unfolding — details may change.
questions.explanation: 'Developing story' senala al oyente que la informacion es PRELIMINAR y puede cambiar en las proximas horas. Formula estandar de honestidad periodistica en tiempo real — protege credibilidad del medio si datos iniciales resultan incorrectos. Muy usada en breaking events (atentados, desastres naturales, elecciones). Registro: universal en TV news US/UK. Colocaciones asociadas: 'we'll bring you updates', 'as more information becomes available', 'we'll continue to follow this closely'. Error hispano: interpretar como historia inventada — nada mas lejos.
examples: This is a developing story — we'll bring you updates as they come in.
We're following a developing situation at the Capitol. → 'situation' variante

questions.statement: The phrase 'It remains to be seen' is common in news to signal uncertainty about outcomes.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'It remains to be seen' es LA formula neutra periodistica para 'aun no sabemos si funcionara/pasara'. Muy usada en analisis politico, economico, geopolitico. Hedging profesional que protege la credibilidad del analista. Estructura gramatical curiosa: passive infinitive ('to be seen') tras 'it remains' — construccion arcaica cristalizada. Alternativas de mismo registro: 'the jury is still out', 'time will tell' (algo mas casual), 'only time will tell' (poetico). Registro: news, editorial, analysis.
examples: It remains to be seen whether the ceasefire will hold beyond the weekend.
Whether the policy will succeed remains to be seen. → inversion sintactica

questions.prompt: Reportas declaraciones del ministro despues de una rueda de prensa.
questions.question: Which is the news-style way to attribute an opinion?
options: Speaking to reporters earlier today, the minister said the reforms would be 'transformative'.
questions.explanation: Formula estandar de atribucion news: (1) circunstancia con gerund ('speaking to reporters'), (2) marker temporal ('earlier today'), (3) fuente identificada ('the minister'), (4) verbo de decir ('said'), (5) reported speech con palabras exactas entrecomilladas ('transformative'). Las comillas destacan las palabras LITERALES del hablante — evita accusaciones de tergiversacion. Registro: NYT/WaPo/Reuters/AP style. Error hispano: 'according to him' es correcto gramaticalmente pero rompe el registro formal news.
examples: In a statement released Tuesday, the company said the results were 'ahead of expectations'.
During his address to the UN, the president called the moment 'historic'. → 'called X' variant

questions.text: The market reacted sharply to the announcement, with major indices closing down more than two percent.
questions.explanation: Reporte financiero estandar. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'reacted sharply' con /tʃ/ + /ʃ/ /riˈæktɪdˈʃɑːpli/; 'closing down' con /ŋd/ cluster /ˈkləʊzɪŋdaʊn/; 'more than' con weak form /mɔːðən/. Colocaciones nativas de finance news: 'reacted sharply' (reaccionar bruscamente — colocacion fija), 'major indices' (indices principales — plural latino), 'closing down X percent' (cerrar en negativo X% — verbo tecnico). 'Indices' es plural latino de 'index' — 'indexes' tambien correcto pero menos formal.
examples: Wall Street rallied on the news, with the S&P closing up 1.8%. → up vs down
Bond yields spiked following the Fed's decision. → 'spike' = subida brusca

questions.prompt: El anchor cierra el segmento con: 'As the story continues to unfold, we'll bring you the latest.'
questions.question: 'The story continues to unfold' means:
questions.explanation: 'Continues to unfold' = eventos siguen desarrollandose, nueva informacion sigue emergiendo. Formula narrativa periodistica que mantiene la atencion del oyente Y senaliza que habra actualizaciones (crea 'story-following behavior'). Metafora textil: 'unfold' es literalmente 'desdoblar' — como quien abre un mapa poco a poco. Colocaciones asociadas: 'as events unfold', 'the situation is unfolding', 'as the story develops'. Registro: universal news broadcast. Error hispano: interpretar como historia terminada (opuesto).
examples: As the story continues to unfold, we'll bring you the latest. → cliffhanger periodistico
The situation continues to unfold as we speak. → 'as we speak' = ahora mismo, live

questions.statement: In news broadcasting, the phrase 'It's understood that' is used when reporters are certain of the facts.
questions.explanation: FALSO — al reves. 'It's understood that' es HEDGING britanico (mas comun en BBC/Guardian que en US) que indica info venida de fuentes NO OFICIALES o preliminares — MENOR certeza que 'confirmed' o 'announced'. Gradiente de certeza descendente: 'confirmed' > 'announced' > 'reported' > 'understood' > 'believed to be'. Error de comprension frecuente: 'understood' suena a 'entendido/aceptado' pero es 'se entiende que — no confirmado oficialmente'. Politica editorial UK: mas suave con hedge que estilo US directo.
examples: It's understood that talks broke down over compensation. → info de fuentes no oficiales
It's understood the CEO will step down within weeks. → precursor de anuncio oficial

questions.target: For a closer look at what this decision means for markets, we're joined now by our economics correspondent, live from London.
questions.explanation: Formula clasica de anchor-to-reporter handover en broadcast news. Estructura triple: (1) transicion tematica ('for a closer look'), (2) verbo de introduccion en passive ('we're joined now'), (3) credencial + ubicacion en vivo ('economics correspondent, live from London'). Ritmo natural: entonacion firme y clara, pausa breve tras 'markets,', enfasis en 'economics correspondent'. 'Live from X' anade credibilidad de reporte en tiempo real. Contracciones: 'we're' obligatoria — 'we are' rompe el ritmo TV. Registro: news broadcast US/UK universal.
examples: For more on this story, let's turn to our Washington correspondent. → variante corta
Joining us now with the latest is our senior political analyst. → inversion sintactica formal
